title: Historical Rhetoric of Non-Cooperation and Constitutional Restitution

sections.title: The Structural Mechanism
sections.content: After the defeat of the 1848–49 Revolution, Ferenc Deák became a leading voice of 'passzív rezisztencia': refusing public office, in places withholding taxes, and holding that decrees issued against the constitution did not bind Hungarian citizens.

sections.title: Rhetorical Application & Stance
sections.content: You know the adverbial participle in *-va/-ve* from B1 Unit 29; historical texts use it often: *Nem hódolva az önkénynek, a nemzet ragaszkodott az 1848-as törvényekhez* (Not bowing to autocracy, the nation clung to the 1848 laws).

sections.title: Patterns in Context
rows: A nemzet elutasította, hogy önként hódoljon a császári pátensnek.
The nation refused to voluntarily submit to the imperial patent.
Az adómegtagadás a passzív ellenállás egyik fontos eszköze volt.
Tax refusal was one important instrument of passive resistance.
Ragaszkodva a közjogi kontinuitáshoz, megőrizték az alkotmányt.
Clinging to public-law continuity, they preserved the constitution.
